stem: A city has 400,000 residents. The transportation department wants to know the mean time that its residents spend commuting each day. Which of the following is the best reason for the department to use a statistical study instead of collecting data from every resident?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Data collected from a sample are always more accurate than data that are collected from every one of the residents in the population
choices.explanation: Collecting data from every individual is not less accurate. It is just usually impractical.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It would be too difficult and costly to collect data from all of the residents, so data from a sample are used to answer the question about the population
choices.explanation: Statistical studies are necessary when the population is too large or too difficult to collect data from every individual.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A statistical study always gives the exact value of the mean commuting time for the population, which a count of every resident would not
choices.explanation: A sample gives an estimate, not the exact value for the population.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A statistical study is required by law whenever the question of an investigation involves more than one thousand people in a city
choices.explanation: No such requirement applies. The reason is that a study of the whole population is not practical.

explanation: A statistical study is used when the population is too large, or collecting data from everyone is too difficult.

stem: The principal of a school with 1,800 students wants to estimate the mean number of hours that students at the school sleep on school nights. The principal surveys 120 students who were randomly chosen. Which of the following correctly identifies the population and the sample?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The population is all 1,800 students at the school, and the sample is the 120 students who were surveyed
choices.explanation: The population is the whole group of interest. The sample is the subset from which data were obtained.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The population is the 120 students who were surveyed, and the sample is all 1,800 students at the school
choices.explanation: These are reversed. The sample is the smaller group that is studied.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The population is the hours of sleep of the students, and the sample is the 120 students who were randomly chosen
choices.explanation: The population consists of the individuals of interest, not the values that are measured.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The population is the principal of the school, and the sample is the 120 students who were surveyed
choices.explanation: The principal collects the data. The population is the students.

explanation: The population is all of the items or individuals of interest (the 1,800 students). The sample is the subset that was studied (the 120).

stem: A town has 6,500 registered voters. A polling firm contacts 400 of the registered voters. Which of the following gives the population size N and the sample size n?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: These are reversed.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: N is the population size and n is the sample size.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: The sample is part of the population. The sizes are not added.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: n is the number contacted, which is 400. 6,100 is the number who were not contacted.

explanation: N is the number in the population (6,500). n is the number in the sample (400).

stem: A researcher planned to investigate whether a tutoring program improves students' scores on a math test. After seeing that the scores had not improved, the researcher decided to ask a different question: whether the program improves students' reading scores. Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The researcher should keep the original question, because an investigative question should have a defined purpose and not be changed based on the results of the analysis
choices.explanation: Changing the question after seeing the data makes the results hard to interpret.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The researcher must change the question, because a study with a result that shows no improvement does not answer any question
choices.explanation: A result of no improvement answers the original question.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The researcher should collect new data on the reading scores, because the data on math scores can answer only the reading question
choices.explanation: The data on math scores answer the original question about math scores.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The researcher may change the question at any time, because a better question is always the one with a result that is significant
choices.explanation: A question should be chosen before the analysis and not by which result looks better.

explanation: An investigative question should have a defined purpose and should not be changed based on the results of the analysis.

stem: Which of the following is an investigative question that can be answered by collecting and analyzing data?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Is mathematics the best subject for a student to study at a high school, college, or university in the future?
choices.explanation: This is an opinion. There is no variable that can be measured.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Do students at a school who eat breakfast have a higher mean score on a morning quiz than students who do not eat breakfast?
choices.explanation: The variables can be measured and the data can be collected and analyzed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Why do some people enjoy listening to music more than other people enjoy listening to music when they study?
choices.explanation: This does not define variables or data that could be collected.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Is it fair for a school to give a quiz to its students at the beginning of the morning on every day of the week, or is it too much?
choices.explanation: This asks about an opinion about fairness. It does not define data to collect.

explanation: A question should be posed so that the required data can be collected and analyzed.

stem: A study of 100 students reports that the mean amount of sleep on a school night was 7.2 hours. Which of the following is a statement of this result in context?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Each of the 100 students in the study slept for exactly 7.2 hours on a school night, which is the mean of the sleep data
choices.explanation: A mean does not mean that every student slept for that long.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The mean was 7.2, which is the value that was found when the data from the students were added and divided by the sample size
choices.explanation: This describes the calculation, but it does not say what the 7.2 is about.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The mean amount of sleep on a school night for the 100 students in the study was 7.2 hours
choices.explanation: It names the variable (sleep on a school night), the group (the 100 students) and the units.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The mean amount of sleep for all of the students in the world on a school night is 7.2 hours, according to the study
choices.explanation: The study included 100 students. It does not give the mean for all students in the world.

explanation: Interpreting in context means relating the number to the variable, the group and the units from the situation.

stem: In a statistical study, what is a collection of data called?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A datum
choices.explanation: A datum is a single piece of information. A collection of data is a data set.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A parameter
choices.explanation: A parameter is a numerical summary of a population.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A population
choices.explanation: A population is all of the items or individuals of interest.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A data set
choices.explanation: A datum is a piece of information about an item or individual. A collection of data is called a data set.

explanation: A collection of data is called a data set.

stem: The table shows some data from a study of students at a school. What is the observational unit in this data set?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The GPA of a student, because it is the numerical variable in the data set and it is measured for every student
choices.explanation: GPA is a variable that is measured on each observational unit. It is not the unit.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A student at the school, because each row of the table gives the data collected from one student
choices.explanation: An observational unit is the item or individual from which a datum is collected.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The school, because all five students in the table were selected from the one school that is in the study
choices.explanation: The data are collected from each student, so the student is the unit.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A grade level, because it is the first variable listed in the table after the names of the students
choices.explanation: Grade level is a variable. It changes from one student to another.

explanation: Each row describes one student, so the observational unit is a student.

stem: A polling firm surveys 400 randomly selected voters in a state and finds that 54% of them support a ballot measure. Which of the following describes the value 54%?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A variable, because it is a characteristic that changes from one voter in the sample to another voter in the sample
choices.explanation: A variable is a characteristic that changes from one unit to another. 54% is a single summary.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A parameter, because it is a percent and all percents describe the whole population from which a sample is taken
choices.explanation: A percent from a sample is a statistic.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A statistic, because it is a numerical summary of a variable for a sample of voters, not for the whole population of the state
choices.explanation: A statistic is a numerical summary for a sample. Here it summarizes the 400 voters.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A parameter, because it is the percent of voters that was found by the polling firm in the study of the state
choices.explanation: A parameter summarizes a population. The 54% describes only the 400 voters.

explanation: A numerical summary of a sample is a statistic.

stem: The school district has 3,200 students. The district reports that the proportion of all of its students who walk to school is 0.18. Which of the following describes the value 0.18?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A categorical variable, because the students either walk to school or they do not walk to school each day
choices.explanation: The variable (how a student gets to school) is categorical, but 0.18 is a summary of it for the population.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A parameter, because it is a numerical summary of a variable for the whole population of students in the district
choices.explanation: The 0.18 summarizes all 3,200 students (the population), so it is a parameter.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A statistic, because it is a number that is between 0 and 1 and is calculated from the data that the district has collected
choices.explanation: Being between 0 and 1 does not make it a statistic. The group is the population.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A statistic, because a proportion is always calculated from a sample of the students in the population
choices.explanation: A proportion can describe a population. Here all of the students are included.

explanation: A numerical summary of a variable for a whole population is a parameter.

stem: A random sample of 150 adults in a city is used to find the proportion of adults who own a bicycle. Which of the following statements about the sample proportion and the population proportion is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The sample proportion is a statistic, and it cannot be used to learn anything at all about the proportion of the population of adults in the city
choices.explanation: Statistics can be used to make inferences about parameters.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The sample proportion is a parameter, because it was found by using a random sample of the adults who live in the city
choices.explanation: A value from a sample is a statistic, even if the sample is random.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The sample proportion is a statistic, and it is always exactly equal to the proportion of the population that is estimated
choices.explanation: A statistic is usually not exactly equal to the parameter.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The sample proportion is a statistic. Its value is often not equal to the population proportion, but it can be used to make inferences about it
choices.explanation: The value of a statistic is often not equal to the parameter, but it may provide the basis for inferences about the parameter.

explanation: A statistic is a summary of a sample. It is often not equal to the unknown parameter but can be used to make inferences about it.

stem: Which of the following variables is categorical?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The number of siblings that a student has
choices.explanation: This is a count, so it is quantitative.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The height of a student, in inches
choices.explanation: This is a measured quantity with units, so it is quantitative.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The time that a student takes to run a mile
choices.explanation: This is a measured quantity with units, so it is quantitative.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The postal code of a student's home address
choices.explanation: A postal code is a label for a group, so it is categorical even though it is written with digits.

explanation: A categorical variable takes values that are category names or group labels, such as postal codes.

stem: Which of the following variables is continuous?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The time, in seconds, that a runner takes to finish a 100-meter race
choices.explanation: A continuous variable can take any value in an interval. Time can be any value between two times.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The number of goals that a soccer team scores in one game of the season
choices.explanation: This can only be a whole number, so it is discrete.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The number of pets that a family in a neighborhood owns at this time
choices.explanation: This can only be a whole number, so it is discrete.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The number of students in a class who are absent today
choices.explanation: This can only be a whole number, so it is discrete.

explanation: A continuous quantitative variable can take any value in an interval. Counts are discrete.

stem: Which of the following variables is quantitative?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The weight, in ounces, of a package that a company ships
choices.explanation: It is a measured amount with units.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The number on the back of the jersey of a basketball player
choices.explanation: A jersey number is a label, so it is a categorical variable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The area code of the telephone number of a customer
choices.explanation: An area code is a label for a region, so it is a categorical variable.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The identification number that a school gives to each student
choices.explanation: An ID number is a label for a student. It is a categorical variable.

explanation: A quantitative variable takes numerical values for a measured or counted quantity. Labels written with digits are categorical.

stem: The table shows data on four dogs. How many of the variables in the table are quantitative?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Four, because the breed and the fence information are values that are recorded for every one of the dogs
choices.explanation: Breed and whether the owner has a fence are categorical.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Three, because the age, the weight, and the name of each dog are all values that can be put in order
choices.explanation: The names are labels, so they are categorical.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Two, because weight and age are measured quantities with units, and the other variables are labels or categories
choices.explanation: Weight (pounds) and age (years) are quantitative.

choices.label: D
choices.text: One, because only the weight of a dog is measured with units while the age is a count of the years
choices.explanation: Age in years is also a quantitative variable with units.

explanation: Weight and age are quantitative. Breed and fence are categorical (and the dog's name is a label).

stem: A biologist records the species and the height, in meters, of each of 60 trees in a forest. Which of the following correctly describes the variables?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both species and height are categorical variables, because the observational units are trees and not people
choices.explanation: Height is a measured quantity, so it is quantitative.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Species is a categorical variable, and height is a discrete quantitative variable because it is recorded in meters
choices.explanation: Height can take any value in an interval, so it is continuous.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Species is a quantitative variable, and height is a categorical variable that can be grouped into short and tall
choices.explanation: Species is a category name, and height is a measurement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Species is a categorical variable, and height is a continuous quantitative variable that can take any value
choices.explanation: Species names are categories. Height is a measurement that can take any value in an interval.

explanation: Species is categorical. Height is a measured quantity that can take any value in an interval: continuous.

stem: In a survey of 200 students, 80 students said that pizza is their favorite lunch. What is the relative frequency of students who chose pizza?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is the relative frequency of the students who did not choose pizza: 120 / 200.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is the frequency (the count), not the relative frequency.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This divides the total by the count. The relative frequency is the count divided by the total.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The relative frequency is the count divided by the total: 80 / 200 = 0.40.

explanation: Relative frequency = 80 / 200 = 0.40.

stem: A relative frequency table for the favorite season of a group of students has the entries 0.35, 0.25, and 0.15 for three of the seasons. The remaining season has no entry. What is the relative frequency for the remaining season?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This repeats one of the entries. The missing one is 1 minus the sum of the entries.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This repeats one of the entries. The missing one is 1 minus the sum of the entries.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is the sum of the three entries, not the remaining relative frequency.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The relative frequencies add to 1, so the remaining one is 1 - 0.35 - 0.25 - 0.15 = 0.25.

explanation: The relative frequencies add to 1: 1 - (0.35 + 0.25 + 0.15) = 0.25.

stem: The table shows how 150 students get to school. What percent of the students chose the category Other?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is 6 / 24, which divides by the count for Walk instead of by the total of 150.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is the percent of the students who chose the bus: 66 / 150. The question asks about the category Other.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This uses the count 6 as a percent. The percent is the count divided by the total, 150.

stem: Among the students in a club who prefer either cats or dogs, the ratio of the number who prefer cats to the number who prefer dogs is 3 to 2. What proportion of these students prefer cats?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is the proportion of the students who prefer dogs.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is the ratio 3 / 2, which is not a proportion because it is greater than 1.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is 2 / 3, the ratio of dogs to cats. The proportion divides by the total of 5.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: 3 of every 5 students prefer cats: 3 / (3 + 2) = 0.60.

explanation: A ratio of 3 to 2 means 3 of every 5: a proportion of 3/5 = 0.60.

stem: In Group A, 60 of 200 students prefer online homework. In Group B, 32 of 80 students prefer online homework. Which of the following is a correct statement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A larger proportion of the students in Group A prefer online homework, because the count of 60 students is greater than the count of 32 students
choices.explanation: The counts cannot be compared directly because the groups have different sizes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A larger proportion of the students in Group A prefer online homework, because Group A has more students in it
choices.explanation: The size of a group does not decide the proportion.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The two groups have the same proportion of students who prefer online homework, because both groups have more than 30 of them
choices.explanation: The proportions are different: 0.30 and 0.40.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A larger proportion of the students in Group B prefer online homework, because 32 / 80 = 0.40 is greater than 60 / 200 = 0.30
choices.explanation: Groups of different sizes should be compared using relative frequencies.

explanation: Compare 60/200 = 0.30 with 32/80 = 0.40: Group B has the greater proportion.

stem: The table shows how 150 students get to school. Which of the following claims is supported by the table?

choices.label: A
choices.text: More students in the survey walked to school than rode in a car, because the walking category comes first in the table
choices.explanation: 42 students rode in a car and 24 walked, so more students rode in a car.

choices.label: B
choices.text: More students in the survey took the bus than took any of the other ways of getting to school, because the bus has the largest count
choices.explanation: 66 is greater than each of the other counts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: More than half of the students in the survey took the bus to school, because the bus has the largest count
choices.explanation: Half of 150 is 75, and 66 is less than 75.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The same number of students walk to school as ride in a car, because both categories have more than 20 students
choices.explanation: 24 students walk and 42 students ride in a car.

explanation: Counts and relative frequencies can justify claims in context: 66 is the greatest count, but it is only 44% of the students.

stem: A relative frequency of 0.28 for a category is equivalent to which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 2.8 out of every 100 observations are in the category

choices.label: B
choices.text: 28 observations are in the category
choices.explanation: That would be a frequency. The relative frequency is a proportion of the total.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 0.28 observations are in the category
choices.explanation: Observations are counted in whole numbers. The relative frequency is a proportion.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 28 out of every 100 observations are in the category
choices.explanation: Proportions, percentages and relative frequencies give the same information: 0.28 = 28%.

explanation: A relative frequency of 0.28 is a proportion of 28%.

stem: A frequency table for the favorite color of 80 children shows 20 for blue. A relative frequency table for the favorite color of 50 adults shows 0.30 for blue. Which of the following is a correct statement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A greater proportion of the children than of the adults chose blue, because the children are more than the adults
choices.explanation: The group sizes do not decide the proportions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A greater proportion of the children than of the adults chose blue, because a count of 20 is greater than 0.30
choices.explanation: A count cannot be compared with a proportion.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A greater proportion of the adults than of the children chose blue, because 0.30 is greater than 20 / 80 = 0.25
choices.explanation: Both are proportions after the count 20 is divided by 80.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The same proportion of the children and of the adults chose blue, because both groups gave a number near 20
choices.explanation: 0.30 is a proportion, and 20 is a count of the children.

explanation: 20 / 80 = 0.25 for the children, which is less than the 0.30 for the adults.

stem: The bar chart shows the favorite lunch of 100 students. How many more students chose pizza than chose salad?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Pizza has a count of 32 and salad has a count of 12, so the difference is 20.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is the number of students who chose salad.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is the number of students who chose pizza.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This adds the counts of the two categories instead of finding their difference.

explanation: 32 - 12 = 20 students.

diagram.altText: Bar chart of the favorite lunch of 100 students.

stem: A pie chart displays the favorite pet of the students in a class. One slice has a central angle of 90 degrees. What relative frequency does this slice represent?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: The angle is not the percentage. The slice is 90 out of 360 degrees.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: A half would be 180 degrees.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This divides 360 by 90. The relative frequency is 90 / 360, which is less than 1.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The whole circle is 360 degrees, and 90 / 360 = 0.25.

explanation: The area of a slice, as a fraction of the whole, is the relative frequency: 90/360 = 0.25.

stem: A pie chart shows four categories of a categorical variable. Three of the slices represent 15%, 25% and 30% of the observations. What percent of the observations does the fourth slice represent?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is the sum of the three slices.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The sum of all four slices must be 100%, so the fourth slice is 100 minus the other three.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: The three slices add to 70%, so the remaining slice is 30%.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The slices of a pie chart add to 100%: 100 - (15 + 25 + 30) = 30.

explanation: The areas of the slices add to 100%.

stem: Which of the following graphs is appropriate for displaying the distribution of a categorical variable such as the favorite sport of the students in a school?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A scatterplot, with each student as a point and the sports placed along the vertical axis of the graph of the study
choices.explanation: A scatterplot shows two quantitative variables.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A boxplot, with a box that shows the median and the quartiles of the sports on the horizontal axis of the display
choices.explanation: A boxplot summarizes a quantitative variable, using a five-number summary.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A bar chart, with a bar for each sport and the height of the bar showing the count or the relative frequency
choices.explanation: Bar charts display the frequencies or relative frequencies of the categories of one categorical variable.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A histogram, with the intervals of the sports along the horizontal axis and the height of each bar showing the count
choices.explanation: A histogram groups the values of a quantitative variable into intervals.

explanation: A bar chart (or a pie chart) displays a categorical variable.

stem: The bar chart shows the relative frequencies of the favorite lunch for the students in Grade 6 and for the students in Grade 8. Which of the following is a correct comparison?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A greater proportion of the Grade 6 students than of the Grade 8 students chose pizza
choices.explanation: The Grade 6 relative frequency for pizza is 0.40, which is greater than 0.25.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A greater proportion of the Grade 8 students than of the Grade 6 students chose pizza
choices.explanation: The Grade 8 bar for pizza is shorter than the Grade 6 bar.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The same proportion of the Grade 6 students and of the Grade 8 students chose tacos
choices.explanation: The bars for tacos are not the same height (0.30 and 0.35).

choices.label: D
choices.text: A greater proportion of the Grade 6 students than of the Grade 8 students chose salad, because the Grade 6 bar is taller
choices.explanation: The Grade 8 bar for salad is taller (0.25 compared with 0.10), so a greater proportion of Grade 8 students chose it.

explanation: Relative frequency bar charts can be used to compare two groups on the same categorical variable.

diagram.altText: Bar charts of the relative frequency of favorite lunch for Grade 6 and Grade 8 students.

stem: The bar chart shows the favorite sport of 140 students. Which of the following claims is supported by the bar chart?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Basketball was the favorite sport of more than half of the students, because it has the tallest bar
choices.explanation: Half of 140 is 70, and 55 is less than 70.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Basketball was the favorite sport of more of the students than any of the other sports, because it has the tallest bar
choices.explanation: The bar for basketball (55) is the tallest.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Soccer and basketball together were the favorite sports of fewer than half of the students in the study
choices.explanation: 40 + 55 = 95, which is more than half of 140.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Baseball was the favorite sport of three times as many students as tennis, because the bar for baseball is the taller one
choices.explanation: Baseball has 30 and tennis has 15, so baseball has twice as many, not three times as many.

explanation: A bar chart can justify claims about a categorical variable in context.

diagram.altText: Bar chart of the favorite sport of 140 students.

stem: Which of the following is a difference between a bar chart and a histogram?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A bar chart displays the categories of a categorical variable, which can be put in any order, and a histogram displays intervals of a quantitative variable in their natural order
choices.explanation: Bars of a histogram stay in the natural order of the numbers. The categories on a bar chart can be rearranged.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A bar chart shows only counts, and a histogram shows only relative frequencies, because the histogram bars cannot show counts
choices.explanation: Both can show either frequencies or relative frequencies.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A bar chart has bars that touch each other, and a histogram has bars that do not touch because the data are numbers
choices.explanation: On a histogram the bars touch. On a bar chart there are usually gaps between the bars.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A bar chart displays a quantitative variable in intervals, and a histogram displays a categorical variable with one bar for each category
choices.explanation: These are reversed.

explanation: Bar charts show categories (in any order). Histograms show intervals of a quantitative variable in order.

stem: In a bar chart of the number of students in each of three clubs, the bar for the Chess club is exactly twice as tall as the bar for the Art club. Which of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Chess club has twice as many students as the Art club, because bar height shows the number of students
choices.explanation: The height of each bar corresponds to the frequency, so a bar that is twice as tall has twice the count.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Chess club has half of the students of the three clubs, because its bar is the tallest bar of the chart
choices.explanation: Twice as tall as the Art club does not mean one half of the total.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Art club has twice as many students as the Chess club, because the shorter bar always shows the larger club
choices.explanation: The taller bar is the larger count.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Chess club has 2 more students than the Art club, because the bar is taller by one unit of the vertical axis
choices.explanation: A bar twice as tall means twice the count, not 2 more.

explanation: The height of each bar corresponds to the frequency (or relative frequency).

stem: The histogram shows the time that each of the students in a class spent on homework one evening. How many of the students spent at least 20 minutes but less than 30 minutes on homework?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is the number of students who spent 20 minutes or more, not just the interval from 20 to 30 minutes.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is the height of the bar for the interval from 30 to 40 minutes.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: The bar for the interval from 20 to 30 minutes has a height of 12.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This is the height of the bar for the interval from 10 to 20 minutes.

explanation: Read the height of the bar for the interval 20 to 30: 12 students.

diagram.altText: Histogram of the time that 40 students spent on homework.

stem: The histogram shows the time that each of the students in a class spent on homework one evening. How many students are in the data set?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: The total number of students is the sum of the heights of the bars: 3 + 8 + 12 + 9 + 5 + 2 + 1 = 40.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is the number of bars (intervals), not the number of students.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is the height of the tallest bar, not the number of students in all of the bars.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This is the largest value on the horizontal axis, not the number of students.

explanation: Add the heights of the bars: 40 students.

diagram.altText: Histogram of the time that 40 students spent on homework.

stem: The histogram shows the time that each of the students in a class spent on homework one evening. How many of the students spent 40 minutes or more on homework?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is only the bar for the interval from 40 to 50 minutes.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is the number of bars that lie to the right of 40 minutes.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is the number of students who spent less than 40 minutes.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Add the bars for 40 to 50, 50 to 60 and 60 to 70: 5 + 2 + 1 = 8.

explanation: 5 + 2 + 1 = 8 students.

diagram.altText: Histogram of the time that 40 students spent on homework.

stem: A histogram of the scores of 100 students on an exam, drawn with bins that are 20 points wide, has one peak. The same data are drawn with bins that are 2 points wide, and the second histogram has several small peaks. Which of the following best explains the difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The mean of the data is different for the two histograms, because the bin width decides the mean
choices.explanation: The bin width does not change the values or the mean of the data.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Changing the bin width can change the appearance of a histogram, even though the data are the same
choices.explanation: Altering the bin widths can change the shape that a histogram appears to have.

choices.label: C
choices.text: One of the two histograms must have been drawn with an error, because the same data cannot give two different shapes
choices.explanation: Both can be correct. The bin width affects how the data are grouped.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The data were changed when the second histogram was drawn, because a histogram with narrower bins uses more values
choices.explanation: Both histograms use the same data. Only the bins are different.

explanation: The choice of bin width changes the appearance of a histogram.

stem: The dotplot shows the number of pets owned by each of 17 students. How many of the students own more than 2 pets?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is the number of students who own 2 pets or fewer.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is the number of students who own 2 pets or more.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is the number of students who own exactly 1 pet.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The values greater than 2 are 3, 3, 4 and 5, which are 4 students.

explanation: Count the dots to the right of 2: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4.

diagram.altText: Dotplot of the number of pets for 17 students.

stem: The stem-and-leaf plot shows the time, in minutes, that each of 12 students took to finish a quiz. How many of the students took more than 30 minutes?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is the number of leaves in the row with the stem 3 only.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The values greater than 30 are 31, 34, 38, 40 and 45.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is the number of students who took 30 minutes or less.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This misses one of the values greater than 30. Count every leaf in rows 3 and 4.

explanation: Rows 3 and 4 have 3 + 2 = 5 leaves.

stem: In a stem-and-leaf plot with the key 2 | 3 means 23 minutes, a row reads 3 | 4 8. Which values does this row represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 34 minutes and 38 minutes
choices.explanation: The stem is the first digit (3) and each leaf is the next digit: 34 and 38.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 3.4 minutes and 3.8 minutes
choices.explanation: The key shows that the stem is the tens digit, so 3 | 4 is 34, not 3.4.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 3 minutes, 4 minutes and 8 minutes
choices.explanation: The row has one stem and two leaves, which give two values.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 7 minutes and 11 minutes
choices.explanation: The leaves are not added to the stem. They are the next digit.

explanation: Each value is the stem followed by its leaf: 34 and 38.

stem: A researcher wants a display of a quantitative data set that shows every individual data value and keeps the values in order from smallest to largest. Which of the following displays does that?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A stem-and-leaf plot, because each value is split into a stem and a leaf and all of the values are shown in order
choices.explanation: Stem-and-leaf plots (and dotplots) show each observation, in order.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A bar chart, because it shows the height of a bar for each of the categories into which the data are placed
choices.explanation: Bar charts are for categorical variables.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A histogram, because it shows the height of a bar for the number of values that are in each interval of the data
choices.explanation: A histogram shows the counts in intervals. The individual values cannot be read.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A pie chart, because it shows the share of the data in each slice of a circle whose total area is 100 percent
choices.explanation: Pie charts are for categorical variables.

explanation: Stem-and-leaf plots and dotplots show the actual values.

stem: The relative frequency histogram shows the ages of the members of a club. What proportion of the members are at least 30 years old but younger than 50 years old?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is only the bar for the interval from 30 to 40 years.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Add the bars for 30 to 40 and 40 to 50: 0.30 + 0.25 = 0.55.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is the proportion of the members who are younger than 30 years.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This is the proportion of the members who are 30 years old or older.

diagram.altText: Relative frequency histogram of ages.

stem: A clinic recorded the waiting time of each of 80 patients. The histogram shows the data. Which of the following best describes the shape of the distribution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Approximately symmetric, because both sides of the histogram have bars that are very tall and very short
choices.explanation: The left half is not a mirror image of the right half.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Approximately uniform, because all of the bars of the histogram have about the same height as one another
choices.explanation: The bars are not all about the same height. The distribution has a peak at small values.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Skewed to the left, because most of the patients waited for a short time and only a few waited for a long time
choices.explanation: A longer tail toward the larger values is skewed right, not left.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Skewed to the right, because the tail extends farther toward the larger values than toward the smaller values
choices.explanation: The right tail (toward larger values) is longer than the left tail.

explanation: The long tail toward larger values means the distribution is skewed right.

diagram.altText: Histogram of waiting times: most values are small, with a long tail to the right.

stem: The histogram shows the scores of 80 students on a quiz. Which of the following best describes the shape of the distribution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bimodal, because the histogram has a tall peak near the large scores and then bars that decrease in height as the scores get smaller
choices.explanation: There is only one main peak, so the distribution is unimodal.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Skewed to the left, because the tail extends farther toward the smaller scores than toward the larger scores
choices.explanation: The left tail (toward smaller values) is longer than the right tail.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Approximately symmetric, because the tallest bars of the histogram are close to the right end of the graph
choices.explanation: A symmetric distribution has halves that are mirror images. This one has a longer left tail.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Skewed to the right, because most of the scores are large and only a small number of the scores are small
choices.explanation: A longer tail toward smaller values is skewed left.

explanation: The longer tail toward smaller values means the distribution is skewed left.

diagram.altText: Histogram of quiz scores: most values are large, with a long tail to the left.

stem: The histogram shows the heights of 80 plants. Which of the following best describes the shape of the distribution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Skewed to the right, because there are a few plants that are much taller than the typical height of the plants
choices.explanation: The right tail is not longer than the left tail.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Approximately uniform, because there are bars at every one of the heights that are shown on the horizontal axis
choices.explanation: The bars are not about the same height. They are tallest in the middle.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bimodal, because the tallest bar is at the center and there is a bar on each side of the center bar
choices.explanation: Bimodal means two prominent peaks. This histogram has one.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Approximately symmetric and unimodal, with one main peak near the middle and the bars falling evenly to each side
choices.explanation: The left half is approximately the mirror image of the right half, and there is one peak.

explanation: One peak in the middle and tails of similar length: approximately symmetric and unimodal.

diagram.altText: Histogram of plant heights: a single peak in the middle with similar tails.

stem: The histogram shows the lengths of the eruptions of a geyser. Which of the following best describes the shape of the distribution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Approximately uniform, because the heights of the bars are never zero for any of the intervals that are shown
choices.explanation: The heights of the bars are not about the same. There are two peaks.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Unimodal, because the histogram has a single group of bars that are tall near the center of the graph
choices.explanation: There are two groups of tall bars with shorter bars between them.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Skewed to the right, because there are bars at the large values that are as tall as those at the small values
choices.explanation: The two peaks have similar heights, so there is no longer tail on one side.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bimodal, because there are two prominent peaks, one at short times and one at long times, with a dip between
choices.explanation: A distribution with two prominent peaks is bimodal.

explanation: Two prominent peaks: a bimodal distribution.

diagram.altText: Histogram with two prominent peaks, one at small values and one at large values.

stem: The histogram shows the wait, in minutes, for a bus for each of 90 riders. Which of the following best describes the shape of the distribution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Unimodal and symmetric, because the bars at the left end are a mirror image of the bars at the right end
choices.explanation: A symmetric unimodal distribution has a peak in the middle. The bars here are about equal.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Skewed to the right, because the bars at the larger values of the wait are the same as those at the smaller values
choices.explanation: A skewed distribution has a longer tail on one side, with tapering bars.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bimodal, because the bars rise and fall several times as the values of the wait get larger across the graph
choices.explanation: There are no two prominent peaks. The differences in height are small.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Approximately uniform, because the bars all have about the same height and there are no prominent peaks
choices.explanation: Each interval has about the same frequency, so the distribution is approximately uniform.

explanation: No prominent peaks and about equal frequencies: approximately uniform.

diagram.altText: Histogram with bars of roughly equal height.

stem: The histogram shows the amount of rain, in millimeters, on each of 41 days. Which of the following is an unusual feature of the distribution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: There are no unusual features, because the histogram has a peak and the heights of the bars decrease after the peak
choices.explanation: The gap and the single large value are unusual features.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The distribution is bimodal, because there is a bar at the large values that is separate from the main group
choices.explanation: A single day does not form a prominent peak. It is a potential outlier.

choices.label: C
choices.text: There are two clusters of data, one cluster for the small values and another cluster for the large values
choices.explanation: There is a single main group and one isolated value, which is not two clusters.

choices.label: D
choices.text: There is a gap between 50 and 90 millimeters, and one day with a much larger value than the other days
choices.explanation: A region with no data is a gap, and a value that is far from the rest is an outlier.

explanation: A gap (no data between the main group and the large value) and an outlier.

diagram.altText: Histogram of rainfall with most values below 50 and one value between 90 and 100.

stem: Which of the following describes a distribution that is skewed to the right?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The distribution has two prominent peaks that are separated by a region of smaller frequencies
choices.explanation: That is bimodal.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The left half of the distribution is approximately the mirror image of the right half
choices.explanation: That is approximately symmetric.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The tail on the right, toward the larger values, is longer than the tail on the left
choices.explanation: Skewed right (positively skewed) means the right tail is longer.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The left tail, toward the smaller values, is longer than the right tail
choices.explanation: That is skewed left.

explanation: A distribution is skewed right if the right tail (toward larger values) is longer than the left.

stem: Which of the following variables is most likely to have a distribution that is skewed to the right?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The annual income of the households in a large city, because a few households have incomes that are much larger than the others
choices.explanation: Income has a lower limit and a few very large values, which creates a long right tail.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The scores of the students on a very easy test, because most of the students have scores that are close to the maximum
choices.explanation: Most scores near the maximum with a few low scores is skewed left.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The result of rolling a fair die many times, because each of the six outcomes has the same chance of occurring
choices.explanation: Each outcome is equally likely, so it is approximately uniform.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The heights of the adult men in a large city, because most of the men have heights that are close to one typical value
choices.explanation: Heights are typically approximately symmetric.

explanation: A variable with a lower limit and a few very large values, such as income, is typically skewed right.

stem: The histogram shows the commute times of 70 workers. Which of the following claims is justified by the histogram?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The workers can be separated into two groups, one with short commutes and another with long commutes
choices.explanation: There is a single main peak, and not two groups.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most of the workers have fairly short commutes, and a few workers have commutes that are much longer than the others
choices.explanation: The tall bars are at the smaller values and there is a long tail to the right.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most of the workers have long commutes, and a few workers have commutes that are much shorter than the others
choices.explanation: The tail extends to the larger values, not the smaller values.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The commute times of the workers are spread evenly over all of the intervals that are shown on the horizontal axis, so there is no peak
choices.explanation: The frequencies are not about equal. They are largest at small values.

explanation: A graph can justify claims in context: here, most commutes are short and a few are very long.

diagram.altText: Histogram of commute times, skewed right.

stem: The data set 8, 12, 9, 25, 14, 10, 11, 15 shows the number of text messages that each of 8 students sent yesterday. What is the mean of the data?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: The sum is 104 and 104 / 8 = 13.0.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This divides the sum by 7 instead of by the number of values, which is 8.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is the median, the average of the two middle values (11 and 12) of the ordered data.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This is the maximum of the data, not the mean.

stem: The data set 23, 41, 18, 35, 29, 52, 27, 33, 38, 30 shows the ages of 10 members of a club. What is the median age?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is only the upper of the two middle values. With an even number of values, average the two middle values.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is the mean of the data, not the median.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is only the lower of the two middle values. With an even number of values, average the two middle values.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The ordered data are 18, 23, 27, 29, 30, 33, 35, 38, 41, 52. With 10 values, the median is the mean of the two middle values, 30 and 33.

stem: The ordered data set 4, 7, 8, 10, 12, 13, 15, 17, 18, 21, 24, 30 has 12 values. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is the third quartile, Q3, not the interquartile range.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is Q3 minus the median (19.5 - 14), which is only the upper part of the middle half of the data.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is the range, the maximum minus the minimum (30 - 4).

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Q1 is the median of the lower half (9) and Q3 is the median of the upper half (19.5), so IQR = 19.5 - 9 = 10.5.

stem: The data set 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 is a sample. A calculator gives several statistics for the data. Which of the following is the sample standard deviation, s?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: The sample standard deviation divides the sum of the squared deviations (40) by n - 1 = 4 and takes the square root: sqrt(10) = 3.16.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is the range, the maximum minus the minimum, not the standard deviation.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This divides by n instead of n - 1. That would be the standard deviation of a whole population.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This is the sample variance, s squared, not the standard deviation.

stem: A student's score on an exam is at the 85th percentile of the scores of all of the students who took the exam. Which of the following is a correct interpretation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: About 85% of the scores are greater than or equal to this student's score, and about 15% are less
choices.explanation: This is reversed. The 85th percentile has 85% of the scores at or below it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: This student's score is 85 points higher than the mean of the scores of the students who took the exam
choices.explanation: A percentile does not give a difference in points.

choices.label: C
choices.text: About 85% of the scores are less than or equal to this student's score, and about 15% are greater
choices.explanation: The pth percentile is the value with p% of the data less than or equal to it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: This student answered 85% of the questions on the exam correctly, which is a score of 85 out of 100
choices.explanation: A percentile is about the position of a score among the scores, not the percent correct.

explanation: The 85th percentile has about 85% of the data at or below it.

stem: The daily high temperatures for a city, in degrees Celsius, have a mean of 20 and a standard deviation of 5. Each temperature is converted to degrees Fahrenheit using F = 1.8C + 32. What are the mean and the standard deviation of the temperatures in degrees Fahrenheit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The mean is 68 and the standard deviation is 9
choices.explanation: The mean is converted the same way as each value (1.8(20) + 32 = 68). The standard deviation is multiplied by 1.8, and adding 32 does not change it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The mean is 36 and the standard deviation is 9
choices.explanation: The mean is also changed by adding 32, so it is 68.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The mean is 20 and the standard deviation is 5
choices.explanation: Changing the units of measurement changes the values of the statistics.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The mean is 68 and the standard deviation is 41
choices.explanation: The standard deviation is not changed by adding 32. It is only multiplied by 1.8.

explanation: Changing units affects the statistics: mean 1.8(20) + 32 = 68, standard deviation 1.8(5) = 9.

stem: A teacher adds 5 points to every student's score on a test. Which of the following correctly describes the effect on the measures of center and variability of the scores?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The mean increases by 5, but the median and the standard deviation and the IQR do not change
choices.explanation: The median also increases by 5.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The mean and the median each increase by 5, and the standard deviation and the IQR do not change
choices.explanation: Adding a constant shifts all of the values and so the measures of center. The spread does not change.

choices.label: C
choices.text: None of the measures changes, because adding the same value to each of the scores does not change their order
choices.explanation: The measures of center change. The order does not.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The mean and the median each increase by 5, and the standard deviation and the IQR each increase by 5
choices.explanation: Adding the same value to every score does not change how spread out the scores are.

explanation: Adding a constant to every value adds it to the mean and median and leaves the standard deviation and IQR unchanged.

stem: A data set has a first quartile of 40, a third quartile of 52, and a maximum value of 74. According to the rule that an outlier is more than 1.5 IQR above the third quartile or below the first quartile, is the maximum value an outlier?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, because 74 is greater than the mean of the first quartile and the third quartile, which is 46
choices.explanation: The rule compares the value with the boundary Q3 + 1.5(IQR).

choices.label: B
choices.text: No, because 74 is less than 52 + 3(12) = 88, which is the upper boundary for an outlier
choices.explanation: The rule uses 1.5 times the IQR, not 3 times.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yes, because the upper boundary is 52 + 1.5(12) = 70 and 74 is greater than 70
choices.explanation: IQR = 52 - 40 = 12. Values above Q3 + 1.5(IQR) = 70 are outliers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No, because the maximum value of a data set can never be an outlier of the values of the data set
choices.explanation: A maximum can be an outlier.

explanation: Upper boundary = Q3 + 1.5(IQR) = 52 + 18 = 70. Since 74 > 70, the maximum is an outlier.

stem: A data set has a mean of 80 and a standard deviation of 6. A value is considered an outlier if it is more than 2 standard deviations above or below the mean. Which of the following values is an outlier?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: 71 is 9 below the mean, which is less than 2 standard deviations.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: 93 is 13 above the mean, which is more than 2(6) = 12.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: 92 is exactly 12 above the mean, which is exactly 2 standard deviations and not more than 2.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: 68 is exactly 12 below the mean, which is exactly 2 standard deviations and not more than 2.

explanation: An outlier is more than 12 from the mean: only 93 qualifies.

stem: Which of the following pairs consists of a resistant measure of center and a resistant measure of variability?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The median and the range
choices.explanation: The range uses the minimum and maximum, so it is not resistant.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The mean and the standard deviation
choices.explanation: Outliers can affect both of these values greatly, so they are not resistant.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The mean and the interquartile range
choices.explanation: The mean is not resistant, because outliers can affect it greatly.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The median and the interquartile range
choices.explanation: Outliers do not greatly affect the median or the IQR.

explanation: The median and IQR are resistant. The mean, range and standard deviation are not.

stem: The largest value in a data set of 15 values is changed from 40 to 400, and no other value is changed. Which of the following summary statistics must stay the same?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The range
choices.explanation: The range is the maximum minus the minimum, so it increases.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The median
choices.explanation: The median is the middle value, which does not depend on how large the largest value is.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The mean
choices.explanation: The mean uses every value, so it increases.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The standard deviation
choices.explanation: The standard deviation uses every value, so it increases.

explanation: The median is resistant to the change in the largest value.

stem: The incomes of the households in a large city have a distribution that is strongly skewed to the right. Which of the following is the better choice of summary statistics to describe the typical income and the variability of the incomes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The median and the IQR, because they are not greatly affected by the very large incomes in the right tail
choices.explanation: For a skewed distribution with outliers, resistant measures describe the data better.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The mean and the IQR, because the mean is a good measure of the center for a distribution of any shape
choices.explanation: The mean is not resistant, so it is pulled toward the long tail.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The range and the standard deviation, because they show how far the largest income is from the smallest income
choices.explanation: Both are affected greatly by very large incomes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The mean and the standard deviation, because they use every one of the values of the incomes in the calculation
choices.explanation: The very large incomes would affect the mean and standard deviation greatly.

explanation: Use the median and IQR when the distribution is skewed or has outliers.

stem: The sample standard deviation of a data set is 4. What is the sample variance?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is the square root of the standard deviation.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is the standard deviation. The variance is its square.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: The variance is the square of the standard deviation: 4 squared = 16.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This doubles the standard deviation instead of squaring it.

explanation: Variance = s squared = 16.

stem: The boxplot shows the scores of 20 students on a test. What is the interquartile range (IQR) of the scores?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is the range, the maximum minus the minimum (78 - 20).

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is the median, the line inside the box.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Q1 is 30 and Q3 is 55, the ends of the box, so IQR = 55 - 30 = 25.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This is the median minus the first quartile (40 - 30), which is only part of the box.

diagram.altText: Boxplot of test scores: minimum 20, Q1 30, median 40, Q3 55, maximum 78.

stem: The boxplot shows the scores of 20 students on a test. About what percent of the students had scores between 30 and 55?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: The first quartile is the 25th percentile and the third quartile is the 75th percentile, so the box contains 50%, not 75%.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The whiskers extend beyond the box to the minimum and maximum. The box has the middle 50% of the data.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Each whisker represents about 25% of the data. The box represents 50%.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The box, from Q1 to Q3, represents the middle 50% of the data.

explanation: Q1 and Q3 form the boundaries of the middle 50% of the values.

diagram.altText: Boxplot of test scores: minimum 20, Q1 30, median 40, Q3 55, maximum 78.

stem: In a boxplot with no outliers, about what percent of the data values are between the third quartile and the maximum?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: About 75% of the data are less than or equal to Q3. The whisker above Q3 has 25%.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Each whisker represents about 25% of the data.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: The whisker above Q3 represents about 25%, not 10%.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: That is the percent of the data in the box, between Q1 and Q3.

explanation: The lines (whiskers) each represent 25% of the data.

stem: The boxplot shows the times, in minutes, that 16 people took to complete a puzzle. The point at 75 is plotted separately from the whisker. Which of the following is the best description of the point?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is the third quartile, because it is the value that is farthest to the right of the median in the boxplot
choices.explanation: The third quartile is the right end of the box.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a typical value, because every value of a data set must be inside the whiskers of a boxplot of the data
choices.explanation: Values beyond the whiskers are outliers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is an outlier, because it is more than 1.5 IQR above the third quartile, so the whisker extends only to the largest value that is not an outlier
choices.explanation: When there are outliers, the whiskers extend to the most extreme values that are not outliers, and the outliers are shown with a symbol.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is the mean of the data, because it is plotted separately from the box and the whiskers on the number line
choices.explanation: The mean is not shown on a boxplot.

explanation: A value more than 1.5 IQR beyond a quartile is an outlier and is plotted separately.

diagram.altText: Boxplot with one point, 75, plotted beyond the upper whisker.

stem: The boxplot shows a data set. The median is closer to the first quartile than to the third quartile, and the upper whisker is much longer than the lower whisker. Which of the following is most likely true about the relationship between the mean and the median?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The mean is less than the median, because the distribution is skewed to the right
choices.explanation: A right skew pulls the mean up, above the median.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The mean is greater than the median, because the distribution is skewed to the right
choices.explanation: If a distribution is skewed right, the mean is usually larger than the median.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The mean is approximately equal to the median, because the box of the boxplot contains the middle 50% of the data
choices.explanation: The mean and median are close only when the distribution is approximately symmetric.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The mean is less than the median, because the upper whisker is longer than the lower whisker of the boxplot
choices.explanation: A longer upper whisker indicates a right skew, which makes the mean larger.

explanation: A long right whisker and a median near Q1 indicate skewed right, so the mean is usually greater than the median.

diagram.altText: Boxplot of a right-skewed variable: the median is near the left of the box and the upper whisker is long.

stem: Which of the following sets of values is the five-number summary that is used to construct a boxplot?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The minimum, the first quartile, the median, the third quartile, and the maximum of the data set
choices.explanation: A five-number summary is made up of these five values.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The first quartile, the second quartile, the third quartile, the fourth quartile, and the range
choices.explanation: The five-number summary includes the minimum and the maximum, not the range.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The mean, the standard deviation, the minimum, the maximum, and the sample size of the data
choices.explanation: A boxplot is not based on the mean or standard deviation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The minimum, the mean, the median, the mode, and the maximum of the values of the data set
choices.explanation: The mean and mode are not part of the five-number summary.

explanation: Minimum, Q1, median, Q3, maximum.

stem: The data set 14, 22, 9, 31, 18, 26, 12, 40, 20, 24 has 10 values. Which of the following is its five-number summary?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: 21.6 is the mean, not the median, and 18 and 24 are not the quartiles.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: These quartiles are not the medians of the lower and upper halves of the ordered data.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Ordered: 9, 12, 14, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 31, 40. The median is (20 + 22) / 2 = 21, Q1 is the median of the lower five values (14), and Q3 is the median of the upper five values (26).

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: 22 is not the median. With 10 values, the median is the mean of the fifth and sixth values (20 and 22), which is 21.

explanation: The five-number summary is 9, 14, 21, 26, 40.

stem: In a boxplot of a data set, the median is in the middle of the box, and the two whiskers have about the same length. Which of the following is the most reasonable conclusion about the distribution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The distribution is uniform, because the two whiskers are the same length and the box is in the middle
choices.explanation: A boxplot cannot show whether a distribution is uniform.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The distribution is skewed to the right, so the mean is much greater than the median of the distribution
choices.explanation: There is no sign of a longer upper whisker or a median near Q1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The distribution is approximately symmetric, so the mean and the median are close to each other
choices.explanation: A median in the middle of the box and equal whiskers indicate symmetry.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The distribution is bimodal, because a boxplot with a median in the middle always has two peaks in the data
choices.explanation: A boxplot does not show the number of peaks.

explanation: A median in the middle of the box and whiskers of similar length suggest an approximately symmetric distribution.

stem: The boxplots show the test scores of the students in Class A and in Class B. Which of the following is a correct comparison of the two distributions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The median scores of the two classes are the same, and the range is greater for Class B than for Class A
choices.explanation: The medians are not the same. Class B has the higher median.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The median score is higher for Class B than for Class A, and the IQR is much greater for Class A than for Class B
choices.explanation: The boxes have similar lengths, so the IQRs are similar.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The median score is higher for Class A than for Class B, and the variability, as measured by the IQR, is similar for the two classes
choices.explanation: The median line of Class B is farther to the right than the median line of Class A.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The median score is higher for Class B than for Class A, and the variability, as measured by the IQR, is similar for the two classes
choices.explanation: Compare the centers (the medians are the lines in the boxes) and the lengths of the boxes (IQR).

explanation: Class B's median (81.0) is greater than Class A's (73.0); the boxes have similar lengths.

diagram.altText: Boxplots of the test scores of two classes.

stem: The table gives summary statistics for the amounts of weight lost, in pounds, by two groups of people who followed two different plans. Which of the following is a correct comparison of the two distributions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The weight losses for Plan 2 are greater than those for Plan 1, because the standard deviation is greater for Plan 2
choices.explanation: A greater standard deviation means more variability, not a greater center.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The weight losses for the two plans are the same, because the means of the two groups are exactly equal to each other
choices.explanation: The variability is different, so the distributions are not the same.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The centers are about the same, but the weight losses for Plan 2 are more variable than the weight losses for Plan 1
choices.explanation: The means and medians are close, while the standard deviation and IQR are larger for Plan 2.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The centers are about the same, but the weight losses for Plan 1 are more variable than the weight losses for Plan 2
choices.explanation: Plan 1 has the smaller standard deviation and IQR, so it is less variable.

explanation: Same center (means about 52), but Plan 2 has the greater standard deviation and IQR.

diagram.caption: Weight loss, in pounds, for two groups of people after 3 months

stem: A student's score on a test is 78. The mean score of the class is 70 and the standard deviation of the scores is 4. What is the z-score of the student's score?

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This divides the standard deviation by the difference (4 / 8). The z-score is the difference divided by the standard deviation.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This divides the score by the standard deviation instead of using the difference from the mean.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This is the difference from the mean. The z-score divides it by the standard deviation.

stem: A runner's time in a race has a z-score of -1.5 among the times of all of the runners in the race. Which of the following is a correct interpretation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The runner's time was 1.5 minutes below the mean time of the runners in the race
choices.explanation: A z-score is a number of standard deviations, not minutes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The runner's time was 1.5 times the mean time of the runners who took part in the race
choices.explanation: A z-score is not a ratio to the mean.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The runner's time was 1.5 standard deviations below the mean time of the runners
choices.explanation: A negative z-score means the value is below the mean. The size is the number of standard deviations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The runner's time was 1.5 standard deviations above the mean time of the runners
choices.explanation: A negative z-score means below the mean.

explanation: A z-score measures how many standard deviations a value is above (positive) or below (negative) the mean.

stem: On the SAT, the scores have a mean of 1050 and a standard deviation of 200. On the ACT, the scores have a mean of 21 and a standard deviation of 5. A student has an SAT score of 1250 and a different student has an ACT score of 27. Which of the following is a correct statement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The student with the SAT score had the better performance relative to the others, because the SAT has the greater standard deviation
choices.explanation: A greater standard deviation does not mean a better relative performance. Compare the z-scores.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The student with the ACT score had the better performance relative to the other test takers, because a z-score of 1.2 is greater than a z-score of 1.0
choices.explanation: z-scores compare relative position: ACT z = (27 - 21) / 5 = 1.2, SAT z = (1250 - 1050) / 200 = 1.0.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The two students had the same performance relative to the others, because each score is above the mean of its own test
choices.explanation: Both are above the mean, but by different numbers of standard deviations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The student with the SAT score had the better performance relative to the other test takers, because 1250 is greater than 27
choices.explanation: The scores are on different scales and cannot be compared directly.

explanation: Compare z-scores: ACT 1.2 is greater than SAT 1.0.

stem: The scores on a test have a mean of 60 and a standard deviation of 8. A student's score has a z-score of 1.25. What was the student's score?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This adds the z-score to the mean. The z-score must be multiplied by the standard deviation first.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is the number of points above the mean. The score is the mean plus 10.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This subtracts 1.25(8) from the mean. A positive z-score is above the mean.

stem: A sample of 50 values has a mean of 50 and a standard deviation of 5. The population mean and standard deviation are not known. Which of the following is the z-score of a value of 60 that is based on the sample statistics?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It cannot be calculated
choices.explanation: The sample mean and standard deviation can be used when the parameters are unknown.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This divides the value by the standard deviation instead of using the difference from the mean.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This divides the standard deviation by the difference. The z-score is the difference divided by the standard deviation.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: When the population mean and standard deviation are unknown, the sample mean and standard deviation may be used: z = (60 - 50) / 5 = 2.

stem: A value in a data set is equal to the mean of the data set. What is the z-score of the value?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: A z-score of -1 would be one standard deviation below the mean.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: A z-score of 1 would be one standard deviation above the mean.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: z = (x - mean) / s = 0, because the value is exactly at the mean.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It depends on the standard deviation
choices.explanation: The numerator is 0, so the z-score is 0 for any standard deviation.

explanation: The value is 0 standard deviations from the mean.

stem: The boxplots show the time, in minutes, that customers took to check out at two stores. Which of the following claims is justified by the boxplots?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The checkout times at Store A are the shorter times, because its boxplot has a longer upper whisker than that of Store B
choices.explanation: A longer upper whisker does not mean shorter times.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Store B has the longer upper whisker and the median closer to the first quartile, so its times are more skewed to the right than the times at Store A
choices.explanation: This describes the pattern of Store A, not Store B.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both stores have the same median checkout time, because the boxplots are drawn on the same number line of times
choices.explanation: The medians are different. Compare the median lines.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Store A has the longer upper whisker and the median closer to the first quartile, so its times are more skewed to the right than the times at Store B
choices.explanation: Boxplots can be used to compare center, variability, outliers and skewness.

explanation: Compare the shapes of the boxplots: Store A's is skewed right.

diagram.altText: Boxplots of the checkout times at two stores.

stem: A researcher wants to know whether the mean time that students at a large high school spend on homework each night is less than 90 minutes. Which of the following is an investigative question that makes clear both the parameter and the direction of the alternative hypothesis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Do the students at the high school spend a lot of time on homework each night during the whole school year?
