choices.explanation: It does not name a parameter or a direction that can be tested.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Is the mean time that students at the high school spend on homework each night less than 90 minutes?
choices.explanation: It names the parameter (the mean homework time for the students at the school) and the direction (less than 90 minutes).

choices.label: C
choices.text: Is the mean time that students at the high school spend on homework each night different from the median time?
choices.explanation: This compares two summaries of the same data. It does not name the parameter and the direction of the question.

choices.label: D
choices.text: What is the time that the first student who is surveyed at the high school spends on homework each night?
choices.explanation: This asks about one student and not about the parameter for the students at the school.

explanation: For a hypothesis test, the question should make clear the parameter and the direction of the alternative.

stem: A city official wants to estimate the proportion of all households in the city that recycle. Which of the following investigative questions guides the choice of a confidence interval?

choices.label: A
choices.text: What is the proportion of all households in the city that recycle, estimated within a range of plausible values?
choices.explanation: For a confidence interval, the question should make clear the parameter and the goal of estimating it within a range of values.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Why do some of the households in the city choose to recycle while some of the other households do not?
choices.explanation: This asks for reasons. It does not name a parameter to estimate.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Is the proportion of all households in the city that recycle greater than the proportion that own a car?
choices.explanation: This compares two proportions and asks for a direction, which guides a test.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Do the households in the city that recycle also have a higher mean income than the households that do not?
choices.explanation: This is a question about a difference between means, which does not name a proportion to estimate.

explanation: A confidence interval question names the parameter and the goal of estimating it within a range of values.

stem: A researcher randomly assigns 80 volunteers to one of two exercise programs and compares the changes in their resting heart rates after 8 weeks. Which of the following is the type of conclusion that can be applied from this study?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Only an association between the programs and the heart rate, because the heart rate was measured after the eight weeks
choices.explanation: Random assignment allows a cause-and-effect conclusion.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A cause-and-effect conclusion about all people in the world, because the 80 volunteers were assigned to the two exercise programs at random in the study of heart rate
choices.explanation: The volunteers were not randomly selected, so the conclusion cannot be applied to everyone.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A cause-and-effect conclusion about the effect of the exercise programs on the resting heart rate, for people who are similar to the volunteers
choices.explanation: Random assignment of treatments allows a cause-and-effect conclusion. The volunteers are not a random sample, so the conclusion applies to similar people.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No conclusion of any kind, because a study that uses volunteers cannot give any information about a population
choices.explanation: The results apply to individuals that are similar to the volunteers.

explanation: Random assignment supports a cause-and-effect conclusion; volunteers limit generalization to similar individuals.

stem: The principal of a school with 800 students asks every one of the students to complete a survey about their lunch preferences. What is this type of study?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An experiment, because the students are asked the same questions and so they are all treated in the same way
choices.explanation: An experiment assigns treatments. Asking questions is a survey, which is an observational study.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A census, because information is recorded from every individual in the population
choices.explanation: A census consists of recording information from all of the items or individuals in a population.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A simple random sample, because every one of the students has the same chance of being included in the survey
choices.explanation: A sample includes only part of the population. Here every student is included.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A cluster sample, because the students of the school are in groups of classes that are surveyed during the day
choices.explanation: All students are surveyed, not a sample of groups.

explanation: Recording information from every member of the population is a census.

stem: A researcher flips a coin for each of 60 patients to decide whether the patient takes a new medicine or a placebo, and then compares the changes in blood pressure of the two groups. Which of the following describes this study?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is a census, because the researcher recorded the blood pressure of every one of the 60 patients in the study
choices.explanation: A census is about the whole population. The 60 patients are not a whole population of interest.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is an observational study, because the blood pressure was recorded for each patient after the medicine was taken
choices.explanation: Recording a response is part of both types of study. Here the researcher imposed the treatments.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is an experiment, because the researcher assigned the treatments to the patients
choices.explanation: In an experiment a researcher assigns conditions, or treatments, to experimental units.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a survey, because the researcher asked each patient a standard set of questions about the medicine
choices.explanation: A survey collects data with a standard set of questions. Here the treatments were assigned.

explanation: The researcher imposed the treatments, so this is an experiment.

stem: A researcher looks at the records of 500 patients, some of whom chose to take a vitamin supplement, and compares the rates of colds of the patients who took the supplement with the rates of the patients who did not. Which of the following describes this study?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is an observational study, because the researcher did not impose the treatments but recorded what the patients chose
choices.explanation: In an observational study treatments are not imposed. The researcher records the values of the variables.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is an experiment, because the researcher recorded a response variable on each one of the 500 patients
choices.explanation: Experiments assign the treatments. Here the patients chose.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is an experiment, because the patients in the records are divided into two groups that are compared by the researcher
choices.explanation: Dividing the data into groups is not the same as assigning treatments.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a census, because the researcher used the records of 500 patients that were recorded in the past
choices.explanation: A census records every member of a population, not just 500 patients.

explanation: Treatments were chosen by the patients, not imposed by the researcher: an observational study.

stem: A farmer assigns 12 plots of land to receive one of three fertilizers, with 4 plots for each fertilizer, and then measures the yield of each plot. Which of the following correctly identifies the experimental units, the treatments, and the response variable?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The experimental unit is the farmer, the treatments are the 12 plots, and the response variable is the fertilizer
choices.explanation: The farmer does not receive a treatment. The plots do.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The experimental units are the 12 plots, the treatments are the yields, and the response variable is the fertilizer
choices.explanation: The yield is the outcome that is measured, so it is the response variable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The experimental units are the three fertilizers, the treatments are the 12 plots, and the response variable is the yield
choices.explanation: The units and the treatments are reversed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The experimental units are the 12 plots, the treatments are the three fertilizers, and the response variable is the yield
choices.explanation: The experimental unit is the unit to which a treatment is assigned. The treatments are the levels of the explanatory variable (fertilizer).

explanation: Plots are the experimental units, fertilizers are the treatments, and yield is the response.

stem: A study selects 500 adults today, and then collects data on their diets now and on their health every year for the next 10 years. Which of the following describes this study?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is a prospective study, because the individuals are selected at one point in time and data are gathered both then and in the future
choices.explanation: A prospective study gathers data at the time of selection and into the future.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is an experiment, because the adults were followed for many years while the same researcher recorded their data
choices.explanation: No treatments are assigned, so it is an observational study.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is a retrospective study, because the individuals are selected now and the data are about their health during the next years
choices.explanation: A retrospective study gathers data from the past.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a census, because all of the adults who were selected were followed for the entire 10 years of the study
choices.explanation: A census includes the whole population. This study follows 500 adults.

explanation: Selecting individuals now and gathering data now and in the future is a prospective study.

stem: An observational study finds that adults who drink coffee every day have a lower rate of a certain disease than adults who do not drink coffee. A researcher suggests that exercise could be a confounding variable. Which of the following is required for exercise to be a confounding variable?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Exercise must have a larger effect on the disease than coffee drinking has on the rate of the disease
choices.explanation: A confounding variable provides an alternative explanation if it is related to both variables. Its size is not the requirement.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Exercise must be a variable that the researcher assigned to the adults who took part in the study of the disease
choices.explanation: In an observational study the researcher does not assign values of variables.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Exercise must be associated with the rate of the disease, but it does not need to be associated with coffee drinking
choices.explanation: A confounding variable must be associated with both variables.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Exercise must be associated with both coffee drinking and the rate of the disease
choices.explanation: To be a confounding variable, a variable must be associated with both the explanatory variable and the response variable.

explanation: A confounding variable is associated with both the explanatory variable and the response variable.

stem: A researcher selects a simple random sample of 200 students from a school of 1,500 students and surveys them. For which population is it appropriate to generalize the results of the survey?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Only the students at the school who are similar to the ones who volunteered, because the survey was a voluntary survey
choices.explanation: The sample was random, not a group of volunteers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Only the 200 students who were surveyed, because a sample cannot be used to describe any students who were not surveyed
choices.explanation: A random sample allows generalizations to the whole population it came from.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All 1,500 students at the school, because the sample was selected from the population using a random mechanism
choices.explanation: When units are randomly selected from a population, it is appropriate to generalize to the whole population.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All of the students at all of the schools in the same state, because a random sample is representative of any school
choices.explanation: The sample was selected only from this school, so the conclusions apply to this school.

explanation: A random sample supports generalizing to the entire population it was selected from.

stem: To choose 30 students from a list of 600 students, a teacher writes each student's name on a slip of paper, mixes the slips in a large box, and draws out 30 slips. What is the sampling method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A systematic random sample, because the slips were taken out of the box one after another in a regular order
choices.explanation: A systematic sample uses a random start and a fixed interval.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A simple random sample, because every possible group of 30 students has the same chance of being the sample
choices.explanation: In a simple random sample of size n, every sample of size n has the same chance of being selected.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A stratified random sample, because the 600 students were put in a single list before the slips were drawn from the box
choices.explanation: Strata are non-overlapping groups, with a simple random sample from each of the groups.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A cluster random sample, because the slips of paper were mixed in one box and a group of them was drawn out
choices.explanation: A cluster sample selects whole groups of students and includes every one of the students in the groups.

explanation: Drawing slips from a well-mixed box gives a simple random sample.

stem: A school has 400 freshmen, 350 sophomores, 300 juniors and 250 seniors. The principal selects a simple random sample of 20 students from each of the four grades and combines the four groups into one sample. What is the sampling method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A simple random sample, because the same number of students was selected from each of the four grades, and each student had the same chance
choices.explanation: In a simple random sample every sample of 80 students has the same chance. Here exactly 20 come from each grade, and a senior (20 of 250) is more likely to be chosen than a freshman (20 of 400).

choices.label: B
choices.text: A systematic random sample, because the principal selected the same number of students from each one of the grades
choices.explanation: A systematic sample uses a random start and a fixed interval.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A stratified random sample, because the population was divided into grades and a simple random sample was selected from each grade
choices.explanation: A stratified sample divides the population into non-overlapping strata, selects a simple random sample from each, and combines them.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A cluster random sample, because each of the four grades was a group of students that was included in the sample
choices.explanation: In a cluster sample, a random sample of the groups is chosen and every individual in the chosen groups is included.

explanation: Dividing the population into strata and taking an SRS within each stratum is a stratified random sample.

stem: A company has 30 delivery trucks. The manager randomly selects 4 of the trucks and inspects every one of the packages in each of the 4 trucks. What is the sampling method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A simple random sample, because the trucks were selected by chance from all of the trucks that the company has
choices.explanation: The packages were not selected individually. Whole trucks were selected.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A stratified random sample, because the packages are divided into groups by truck and some packages are inspected from each of the groups
choices.explanation: In a stratified sample, a sample is taken from every stratum. Here only 4 of the trucks were used.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A systematic random sample, because the trucks were inspected one after another with the same procedure
choices.explanation: A systematic sample uses a random start and a fixed interval.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A cluster random sample, because a random sample of groups (trucks) was selected and every unit in the selected groups was observed
choices.explanation: A simple random sample of clusters is selected and data are collected from all of the units in each selected cluster.

explanation: Randomly choosing groups and observing every unit in them is a cluster random sample.

stem: A quality inspector chooses a random starting point among the first 10 items that come off a production line, and then inspects every 10th item after that starting point. What is the sampling method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A simple random sample, because the starting point of the inspector was chosen at random from the first 10 items
choices.explanation: Not every group of items has the same chance. The items after the start are determined.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A stratified random sample, because the items were divided into groups of 10 before one item was chosen from each
choices.explanation: A stratified sample has a simple random sample in each of the strata, which are groups of similar items.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A systematic random sample, because the items are selected using a random start and a fixed interval
choices.explanation: A systematic random sample has a random starting point and a fixed, periodic interval.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A cluster random sample, because the inspector examined the items that were in several groups of 10 items
choices.explanation: A cluster sample includes every unit in the selected clusters. Here only one item in 10 is inspected.

explanation: A random start with a fixed interval is a systematic random sample.

stem: Which of the following describes a difference between a stratified random sample and a cluster random sample?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In a stratified sample, every unit in each selected group is observed, and in a cluster sample, a simple random sample is taken from every group
choices.explanation: These are reversed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A stratified sample is always a larger sample than a cluster sample, because it must include every individual in the population
choices.explanation: Neither method requires a sample that includes everyone.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In a stratified sample, a simple random sample is taken from every stratum, and in a cluster sample, a simple random sample of the clusters is taken and every unit in each selected cluster is observed
choices.explanation: These are the definitions of the two methods.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In a stratified sample, the groups should be as different from each other as possible, and in a cluster sample, the groups should be alike inside
choices.explanation: Strata are groups of similar individuals, and clusters should each be like the whole population.

explanation: Stratified: SRS within every stratum. Cluster: SRS of clusters, then every unit in each selected cluster.

stem: In which of the following is an observational unit selected without replacement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A student is chosen by a random number generator that may give the same number for more than one of the draws
choices.explanation: If a number can repeat, the units are selected with replacement.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A name is drawn from a hat, and it is not put back before the next name is drawn, so no one can be chosen twice
choices.explanation: In sampling without replacement a unit can be selected only once.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A name is drawn from a hat, and it is put back in the hat before the next name is drawn, so a name can be chosen twice
choices.explanation: This is sampling with replacement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A card is drawn from a deck, and the card is returned to the deck and shuffled before the next of the draws
choices.explanation: Returning the card to the deck is sampling with replacement.

explanation: Sampling without replacement means a unit can be selected only once.

stem: A population has 10 individuals. A sampling method selects a sample of 2 individuals by choosing individual number 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 at random, and then always selecting the individual who is 5 places after the first one. Which of the following is true about the method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The method is a simple random sample, because the first individual that was selected was chosen by a random mechanism
choices.explanation: Only the first individual is chosen at random. The second one is determined.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The method is not random, because the first individual in the sample is not chosen with the help of any random mechanism
choices.explanation: The first individual is chosen at random.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The method is a simple random sample, because every one of the individuals has the same chance of being in the sample
choices.explanation: Equal chances for individuals are not enough. Every sample of size 2 must have the same chance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every individual has the same chance of being selected, but the method is not a simple random sample, because some pairs of individuals can never be the sample
choices.explanation: In a simple random sample every sample of size n has the same chance. Here pairs that are not 5 apart are impossible.

explanation: A simple random sample needs every sample of size n to be equally likely. This is a systematic-type method.

stem: A teacher wants to select a simple random sample of 25 students from a list of 400 students. Which of the following describes a correct procedure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Select the 25 students who volunteer first when the teacher asks for volunteers from the whole group of 400 students
choices.explanation: A sample of volunteers is not selected using a random mechanism.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Choose the first 25 students on the alphabetical list, because the order of the names of the students in a list is random, so they are a fair sample of the 400
choices.explanation: The first 25 names are not selected using a random mechanism.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Number the students from 1 to 400, and then use every 16th student, starting from the student with the number 1
choices.explanation: This is a systematic method with a fixed start. It is not a simple random sample.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Number the students from 1 to 400, use a random number generator to select 25 different numbers from 1 to 400, and use the students with those numbers
choices.explanation: Assign each individual a number, and randomly select n different numbers.

explanation: A random number generator applied to a numbered list gives a simple random sample.

stem: The manager of a mall wants to survey shoppers and wants to make sure that adults younger than 30, adults from 30 to 59, and adults 60 or older are all represented in the sample in proportion to their numbers. Which of the following sampling methods is the most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A cluster random sample, with the three age groups as the clusters to be selected one at a time by the manager
choices.explanation: A cluster sample could leave out entire age groups.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A stratified random sample, because the three age groups are the strata and a random sample is selected from each
choices.explanation: A stratified sample guarantees that each stratum is represented in the sample.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A simple random sample, because it always has exactly the same percent of each age group as the whole population has
choices.explanation: A simple random sample does not guarantee the same percent of each of the groups.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A convenience sample of the shoppers who walk by the manager, since they are of all of the ages of the group
choices.explanation: A convenience sample is not random and does not control the representation of the age groups.

explanation: To represent each of the groups, use a stratified random sample.

stem: A school wants to survey its students, who are organized in 40 homerooms of similar composition and size. To save time, the school wants to visit only some of the homerooms. Which of the following sampling methods is the most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A cluster random sample, in which several homerooms are selected at random and every student in each of the selected homerooms is surveyed
choices.explanation: Clusters that are similar to one another and to the population make a cluster sample appropriate and convenient.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A stratified random sample, in which one student is surveyed in each of the homerooms that are in the school
choices.explanation: This visits every homeroom, which does not save time in visiting only some of them.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A systematic random sample, in which the students are surveyed in the order in which they arrive at the school
choices.explanation: That would not limit the survey to some of the homerooms.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A convenience sample, in which the homerooms that are closest to the office are chosen to be in the survey
choices.explanation: Choosing the closest homerooms is not random.

explanation: When clusters are similar to the population, selecting some clusters at random saves effort.

stem: A radio station asks its listeners to call in to say whether they support building a new stadium. Of the 800 callers, 72% say they are against it. Which type of bias is most likely to affect this result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nonresponse bias, because many of the people who were chosen to be in the sample did not give any response
choices.explanation: No one was chosen. Listeners decided for themselves to call.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Response bias, because the question in the survey that the radio station asked of the callers was written in a leading way
choices.explanation: Nothing in the description says that the question was leading.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Undercoverage bias, because the listeners who have a telephone are the only people who are included in the survey
choices.explanation: Undercoverage is about a part of the population that has no chance of being included. The main issue here is that the callers volunteered.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Voluntary response bias, because the sample consists only of listeners who chose to call in
choices.explanation: Voluntary response bias may occur when a sample consists entirely of volunteers, who often have strong opinions.

explanation: A sample that consists entirely of volunteers may suffer from voluntary response bias.

stem: A researcher wants to estimate the proportion of all adults in a large city who use public transportation. The researcher selects a simple random sample of the telephone numbers in the city's landline telephone directory and calls them. Which of the following is the most likely source of bias?

choices.label: A
choices.text: There is no source of bias, because the telephone numbers were selected from the directory using a simple random sample
choices.explanation: A random selection from a list that leaves out part of the population can still be biased.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Response bias, because adults are always less honest with a researcher who calls them on the telephone
choices.explanation: Nothing suggests that the questions are leading, or that adults answer dishonestly.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Voluntary response bias, because the adults who were called decided to answer the telephone for the researcher
choices.explanation: The numbers were selected at random. The adults did not volunteer to be in the sample.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Undercoverage bias, because adults who do not have a landline telephone listed in the directory have no chance of being selected
choices.explanation: Undercoverage bias may occur when part of the population is left out of the sampling method or is less likely to be selected.

explanation: Using a landline directory leaves out part of the population: undercoverage.

stem: A school mails a survey to 1,000 randomly selected parents. Only 120 of the surveys are returned. Which of the following is the most likely source of bias?

choices.label: A
choices.text: There is no source of bias, because the 1,000 parents were selected at random and a random sample has no bias
choices.explanation: Nonresponse can bias even a random sample.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Voluntary response bias, because the parents who sent the survey back chose to take part in the study
choices.explanation: The parents were randomly selected, so they did not volunteer to be in the sample. The main problem is that most of the selected parents did not respond.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nonresponse bias, because the parents who returned the survey may differ in important ways from the parents who did not
choices.explanation: Nonresponse bias may occur because of a failure to obtain responses from some individuals who were chosen.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Undercoverage bias, because some of the parents in the school were not included in the list from which the sample was selected
choices.explanation: The 1,000 parents were selected from the parents. The main problem is that most of them did not respond.

explanation: The respondents and nonrespondents could differ in important ways: nonresponse bias.

stem: A survey asks, "Do you agree that the city's wonderful new park is an excellent use of tax money?" Which type of bias is most likely to result from the wording of this question?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Response bias, because the wording of the question leads respondents to answer in one direction
choices.explanation: Questions that are confusing or leading (question wording bias) can cause responses to differ from the true value in one direction.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nonresponse bias, because many residents who are asked the question will refuse to give any answer at all
choices.explanation: The wording of the question is the problem, not a failure to respond.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Undercoverage bias, because some residents who live in the city will not see the question of the survey
choices.explanation: Undercoverage is about who can be selected. The problem here is the wording.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Voluntary response bias, because respondents who like the park will choose to answer the question in the survey
choices.explanation: The problem is the leading wording, not a sample of volunteers.

explanation: A leading question is a source of response bias.

stem: A researcher asks a random sample of adults how many hours they exercise each week. Many of the adults in the sample report more exercise than they actually do. Which of the following best describes this problem?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sampling error only, because the amount of the exercise differs from one random sample of the adults to another
choices.explanation: The responses are consistently too large, which is a systematic error, not random variation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Undercoverage bias, because the adults who exercise the most are not included in the list that was used to select the sample
choices.explanation: The problem is not a part of the population that was left out. It is the accuracy of the answers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Response bias, because the self-reported answers tend to differ from the true values in one direction
choices.explanation: Self-reported responses are an example of response bias.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Voluntary response bias, because the adults who exercise are the ones who answer questions about their exercise
choices.explanation: The adults were selected at random. They did not volunteer.

explanation: Self-reported responses that tend to differ from the truth in one direction are response bias.

stem: To estimate the proportion of students at a school who own a smartphone, a researcher stands at the school's main door and asks the first 50 students who arrive. Which of the following is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The method is a stratified random sample, because the students at the door arrive in groups by grade level
choices.explanation: Strata require a simple random sample within each of the groups.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The method is a simple random sample, because the students were selected without the researcher knowing who they were
choices.explanation: Not knowing who will arrive does not make the selection random.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The method is not biased, because the proportion of students who own a smartphone cannot depend on when they arrive
choices.explanation: The students who arrive first may differ, and the method does not use random chance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The method is a convenience sample, which is not random, so students who arrive early may differ from the others
choices.explanation: Nonrandom sampling methods, such as samples chosen by convenience, introduce potential bias.

explanation: A convenience sample does not use random chance, so it has potential bias.

stem: Which of the following describes bias in a sampling method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The difference between the value of a statistic for one sample and its value for another sample that is selected from the same population, which is called sampling variability
choices.explanation: This is the natural variation from sample to sample, not bias.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Any mistake in recording the data, such as typing an incorrect value for one of the observations in the sample
choices.explanation: A recording mistake is not a systematic error of the sampling procedure.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A systematic error that results in a statistic being consistently larger, or consistently smaller, than the parameter it is used to estimate
choices.explanation: Bias is a systematic error in the sampling procedure.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The error that results from a sample that is too small, so that a statistic is not exactly the same as the parameter
choices.explanation: A small sample causes more variability, but bias is a systematic error that does not average out.

explanation: Bias is a systematic error in the sampling procedure that makes a statistic consistently too large or too small.

stem: An online poll about a political issue receives 50,000 responses from people who chose to visit the website and vote. A student says that, because the sample is so large, the poll results must be a good estimate of the opinion of all adults. Which of the following is the best response to the student?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The student is correct, because a sample of 50,000 responses is far larger than the samples that most polls use
choices.explanation: The number of responses does not make the sample representative.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A large sample does not remove bias. The sample consists of volunteers, so the results may not represent all adults
choices.explanation: Nonrandom sampling methods, such as voluntary response, introduce potential bias that a larger sample does not remove.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The student is correct, because the larger a sample is, the smaller the bias of the results of a poll will be
choices.explanation: Increasing the sample size does not reduce bias from a poor sampling method.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The student is incorrect, because an online poll can never be used to estimate the opinions of any group of people
choices.explanation: The problem is the voluntary response method, not the Internet.

explanation: A large nonrandom sample still has bias.

stem: A researcher surveys only members of a gym about how often they exercise, and uses the result to estimate the proportion of all adults in the city who exercise at least three times a week. Which of the following is the most likely effect on the estimate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The estimate is likely to be consistently larger than the true proportion, because gym members are more likely to exercise than the other adults
choices.explanation: The method leaves out people who are less likely to exercise, so the statistic tends to be too large.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The estimate is equally likely to be too large as it is to be too small, because the gym members are a random group of adults
choices.explanation: Gym members are not a random group, and the error is in one direction.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The estimate has no bias, because every gym member was included in the survey that the researcher conducted
choices.explanation: Including every gym member does not make the sample represent all of the adults.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The estimate is likely to be consistently smaller than the true proportion, because gym members have less free time to exercise than other adults do
choices.explanation: Nothing indicates that gym members exercise less often.

explanation: The sampling method leaves out adults who are less likely to exercise, so the estimate is biased high.

stem: A researcher gives all 40 of the participants in a study a new fertilizer for their garden plants and records the growth of the plants. Which element of a well-designed experiment is missing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A sample, because a sample of 40 participants cannot be used in an experiment that is designed to compare treatments
choices.explanation: Experiments are conducted with groups of experimental units.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A comparison of at least two treatment groups, such as a group that gets the new fertilizer and a control group that does not
choices.explanation: A well-designed experiment compares at least two treatments, one of which could be a control group.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A response variable, because the growth of the plants is not a quantity that the researcher can measure in a garden
choices.explanation: The growth of the plants is a measurable response variable.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Replication, because a study with 40 participants has too few participants to apply the treatment more than once
choices.explanation: There are 40 participants, so the treatment is applied to more than one experimental unit.

explanation: With only one treatment group there is nothing to compare with.

stem: In a study of a new pain medicine, one group of patients takes the medicine and another group takes a pill that has no active ingredient. What is the purpose of the group that takes the pill with no active ingredient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is a control group that provides a comparison, so that any effect of the medicine can be separated from the effect of simply taking a pill
choices.explanation: A control group may be given an inactive substance (a placebo) to determine whether the treatment of interest has an effect.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It makes sure that every patient in the study has the same chance of getting the new medicine, so that the two groups are alike at the start of the study
choices.explanation: That is the purpose of random assignment, not of a placebo group.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It increases the number of patients in the study, so that the medicine can be tested on many more patients
choices.explanation: The group is for comparison. It is not just for adding more patients.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It makes the study a double-blind study, because the patients in the group do not take any of the active medicine
choices.explanation: Blinding refers to who knows which treatment is received, which is a separate part of the design.

explanation: A placebo control group is used for comparison.

stem: In an experiment, the patients do not know which treatment they receive, but the doctors who give the treatments and measure the results do know. Which of the following describes this experiment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is a single-blind experiment, because the participants do not know which treatment they receive but members of the research team do
choices.explanation: In a single-blind experiment the participants do not know the treatment, but the research team members who interact with them do.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a placebo experiment, because the patients do not know the treatment and the doctors do know the treatment
choices.explanation: A placebo is an inactive treatment. Blinding is about who knows the treatments.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is not blind at all, because the doctors know which treatment each of the patients receives in the experiment
choices.explanation: The patients do not know, so the experiment is single-blind.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a double-blind experiment, because the patients do not know which of the treatments they have been given
choices.explanation: In a double-blind experiment neither the participants nor the research team members who interact with them know.

explanation: Only the participants are blinded: a single-blind experiment.

stem: What is the main purpose of the random assignment of treatments to experimental units in an experiment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To make sure that the experimental units in the study are representative of a larger population of units
choices.explanation: That is the purpose of random selection from a population.

choices.label: B
choices.text: To make sure that the experimenters and the participants cannot know which of the treatments each unit receives
choices.explanation: That is the purpose of blinding.

choices.label: C
choices.text: To create treatment groups that are as similar as possible with respect to extraneous variables, so the groups differ only by the treatment
choices.explanation: If random assignment is successful, the distributions of each extraneous variable will be approximately the same in all of the treatment groups.

choices.label: D
choices.text: To make sure that each treatment is applied to exactly one experimental unit, so that the result can be compared
choices.explanation: Each treatment should be applied to more than one unit (replication).

explanation: Random assignment creates groups that are similar with respect to extraneous variables.

stem: A teacher tests a new study method. Students in a morning class use the new method, and students in an afternoon class use the usual method. The students in the morning class score higher on the next test. Which of the following is a confounding variable in this study?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The time of day of the class, because it is related to the study method that each class used and could also affect the scores
choices.explanation: A confounding variable is related to the explanatory variable in a way that makes it hard to tell which variable influences the response.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The test score, because it is the outcome that the teacher measured for each of the students in the classes
choices.explanation: The score is the response variable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The number of students in each class, because it is the same for the two classes that were in the study
choices.explanation: A variable that is the same for both groups cannot explain a difference between them.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The study method, because it is the treatment that the teacher chose for each one of the two classes
choices.explanation: The study method is the explanatory variable.

explanation: The time of day goes together with the method, so its effect cannot be separated from the effect of the method.

stem: In an experiment, replication means which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The same experimental unit receives each treatment more than one time during the experiment
choices.explanation: That describes repeated measurements on one unit, not replication.

choices.label: B
choices.text: More than one experimental unit is assigned to each treatment, rather than a single unit
choices.explanation: Replication means more than one experimental unit is assigned to each treatment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The experiment is repeated by other researchers in different locations on a later date
choices.explanation: That describes a repetition of the whole study by other researchers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Each experimental unit is given a treatment that has been used in an earlier experiment by the researcher
choices.explanation: Replication is about the number of units per treatment.

explanation: Replication means that more than one experimental unit is assigned to each treatment.

stem: In an experiment on plant growth, the researcher keeps the amount of water, the type of soil and the temperature of the room the same for every plant. Which element of a well-designed experiment does this describe?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Replication of each treatment on several of the plants
choices.explanation: Replication means using more than one unit for each treatment.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Random assignment of the treatments to the plants
choices.explanation: Random assignment uses chance to decide which unit gets which treatment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Blocking of the plants into groups that are similar
choices.explanation: Blocking groups similar units and randomizes treatments within each of the groups.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Direct control of potential extraneous sources of variation
choices.explanation: Direct control keeps the settings of extraneous variables the same from one experimental unit to another.

explanation: Keeping extraneous variables the same for all of the units is direct control.

stem: A researcher has 60 volunteers. The researcher uses a random number generator to assign 20 of the volunteers to each of three diets, with no other grouping of the volunteers. Which of the following experimental designs is this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A matched pairs design, because the volunteers were assigned in equal numbers to the diets of the study
choices.explanation: A matched pairs design has two treatments and pairs of similar units.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A randomized block design, because the volunteers were divided into three groups for the three different diets
choices.explanation: Blocks are groups of similar units that are formed before the treatments are randomly assigned within each block.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A completely randomized design, because the treatments are assigned to the volunteers completely at random
choices.explanation: In a completely randomized design, treatments are assigned to experimental units completely at random.

choices.label: D
choices.text: An observational study, because the researcher is working with a group of volunteers who chose to take part
choices.explanation: The researcher assigned the diets, so this is an experiment.

explanation: Randomly assigning treatments to all of the units without grouping is a completely randomized design.

stem: A researcher believes that the effect of a medicine may be different for men and for women. The researcher separates 60 men and 60 women into two groups, and within each group randomly assigns half to the medicine and half to a placebo. Which of the following describes the design and the purpose of the grouping?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is a randomized block design with sex as the blocking variable, and blocking allows the treatments to be compared without variation from the blocking variable
choices.explanation: In a randomized block design, units are grouped by a blocking variable, and treatments are randomly assigned within each block.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a matched pairs design, because there are two treatments that are given to two groups of volunteers
choices.explanation: Matched pairs arranges units into pairs, and each pair gets both treatments.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is a randomized block design, and the grouping by sex is used to blind the volunteers to the treatment they get
choices.explanation: Blocking is not used for blinding.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a completely randomized design, and the grouping by sex is used to make the volunteers a random sample
choices.explanation: In a completely randomized design there is no grouping before the assignment.

stem: A company wants to compare two brands of running shoes. Each of 25 runners runs a race in one brand of shoe and, on another day, in the other brand of shoe. A coin flip decides which brand each runner wears first. Which of the following describes the design?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is an observational study, because the runners are free to choose which brand of shoe they wear on the first day
choices.explanation: The coin flip, not the runner, decides, so this is an experiment.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a randomized block design with 25 treatments, because there are 25 runners in the study of the two brands
choices.explanation: There are two treatments, so the design with blocks of pairs is a matched pairs design.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is a completely randomized design, because a coin flip is used to decide the treatment of each of the runners
choices.explanation: In a completely randomized design each unit receives only one treatment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a matched pairs design, because each runner receives both treatments and the order of the treatments is randomized
choices.explanation: In a matched pairs design each experimental unit may get both treatments while the order of the treatments is randomized.

explanation: Each runner gets both treatments in a random order: matched pairs.

stem: A well-designed experiment finds that the mean response is greater for the treatment group than for the control group. Which of the following conclusions is justified by the use of random assignment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The treatment would cause the same difference for every individual in the population from which the units were selected
choices.explanation: The conclusion about the population depends on how the units were selected.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The difference in the responses must be due to chance alone, because the units were assigned to the groups using chance
choices.explanation: Random assignment does not mean that a difference is due to chance.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The treatment caused the difference, but this cannot be a cause-and-effect conclusion, because no experiment can show cause and effect
choices.explanation: A well-designed experiment can show cause and effect.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The difference in the responses was caused by the treatment, because random assignment reduces the potential for confounding variables
choices.explanation: Random assignment of treatments allows cause-and-effect conclusions.

explanation: Random assignment allows cause-and-effect conclusions.

stem: Researchers recruit 100 volunteers for an experiment, and randomly assign 50 to a new exercise program and 50 to a control group. The group with the program lowers its blood pressure more. For which of the following is it appropriate to conclude that the program causes a lowering of blood pressure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Only the 50 volunteers in the group that took the program, because the control group did not get the program
choices.explanation: The comparison of the two groups supports the conclusion for similar volunteers, not just one group.

choices.label: B
choices.text: People who are similar to the volunteers, because the treatments were randomly assigned but the volunteers were not randomly selected
choices.explanation: The experimental units were obtained from volunteers, so the results represent experimental units similar to those who took part.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All adults in the country, because the volunteers were assigned to the treatments by the use of chance
choices.explanation: Random assignment supports cause and effect. It does not support generalizing to all adults.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nobody, because a study that uses volunteers cannot support a cause-and-effect conclusion about any group of people
choices.explanation: Random assignment still supports cause and effect for similar individuals.

explanation: Volunteers limit generalization to similar individuals; random assignment allows cause and effect.
